definitions.explanation: The small metal tab you lift to open a drink can. Strictly the modern stay-on tab, though Japanese uses the word for the detachable rings of older cans as well.

examples.japanese: プルタブ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}いて→引く：01978_hiku⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧。
examples.english: Pull the tab to open it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{爪|つめ}→爪：02159_tsume⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{割|わ}れ→割れる：00907_wareru⟧そうでプルタブ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}けられない→開ける：00563_akeru⟧。
examples.english: I can't get the pull tab open without breaking a nail.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小学校|しょうがっこう}→小学校：01055_shougakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧いす⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{寄付|きふ}する→寄付する：20661_kifusuru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧プルタブ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いている→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: At elementary schools, the drive to collect pull tabs to donate wheelchairs still goes on.

notes:
From English "pull tab." The maker's own term is ⟦{缶|かん}→缶：01076_kan⟧{蓋|ぶた} or ステイオンタブ, but ordinary speech uses プルタブ for any drink-can opener tab.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- プルタブ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}く→引く：01978_hiku⟧ / ⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧: to pull / open the tab
- プルタブ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧: to collect pull tabs (for charity)
- プルタブ{式|しき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{缶|かん}→缶：01076_kan⟧: a pull-tab can

CULTURAL NOTE:
Collecting プルタブ to trade for wheelchairs is a long-running school and workplace charity activity in Japan, familiar enough that the phrase プルタブ{集|あつ}め needs no explanation — even though recycling the whole can is now generally more effective.
